$what: CANONICAL OUTPUT of every raster preset aeon actually ships, as Aurora's writer produced it under the schema blob this repo carried BEFORE the re-vendor named in $how_it_was_produced. test/formats/effects-preset-boundary.test.ts asserts the writer still produces exactly these bytes. ⚠ EXCEPT for the ids in unmeasurable_under_previous_schema — read that field before quoting this one.
$why: A re-vendor is exactly the change that can move canonical output for a document nobody touched, because serializeEffectsPreset runs canonicalizeBySchema over the WHOLE document against the WHOLE schema. 'Nothing shipped carries the key, so nothing is refused' is a claim about REFUSAL and says nothing about BYTES. Opening an untouched preset and saving it must not rewrite it; this file is what makes that a measurement instead of an assumption, at this re-vendor and at every one after. ⚠ A BREAKING re-vendor is the case this fixture is WEAKEST on: the document whose own shape migrated has no before-half at all, and saying which one that is (unmeasurable_under_previous_schema) is the difference between a fixture that reports its coverage and one that quietly stops covering the interesting document.
$how_it_was_produced: Generated by scratchpad/regen-preset-canonical-golden.mts (see its header). `documents` are aeon's bytes at origin/master f8beaad0d1ca28fa17d37fb9ee2022bb33a84a9e, read through git OBJECTS and never the sibling working tree. `canonical` is those documents through canonicalizeBySchema + canonicalJsonPretty (src/core/formats/effects/json-schema-subset.ts and src/core/formats/canonical-json.ts, the two modules a preset re-vendor does not touch) under the PREVIOUS vendored schema blob 0295b21b9f60e48685aff245695eaf7dc445ad59; the same run was repeated under the CURRENT blob 8a23b03e023fc9c39adaa1bfa057a1f160b0e4cd and every measured output was byte-identical, which is the finding this fixture preserves. The generator is deliberately NOT built on preset.ts, which at the current revision reads $defs.base_swap.items and cannot load the previous schema at all - so a naive before/after would have compared the new codec to itself.
$not_a_claim_about_aeon: `documents` are aeon's bytes and `canonical` are AURORA's. They differ: aeon's generator writes its own key order, Aurora's writer sorts recursively (aeon docs/EDITOR_RASTER_PRESETS.md section 5, json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2)). This file does NOT assert the two agree, and no row may read it that way. It asserts only that AURORA's answer has not moved.
$re_generate: Only when a re-vendor legitimately changes canonical output - which is a migration of every shipped preset and needs saying out loud, not a fixture refresh. Re-read the header of the row that consumes this before touching it.
$unmeasurable_under_previous_schema: IDS LISTED IN `unmeasurable_under_previous_schema` HAVE NO BEFORE-HALF, AND THEIR `canonical` ENTRY IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THE AMENDMENT. A document whose own SHAPE migrated in the same re-vendor is REFUSED by the previous schema, so canonicalizeBySchema never descends into the migrated key and its output falls through unchanged - which reads as "identical under both" and measures nothing. Those ids are canonicalised under the CURRENT schema and recorded here with the reason, rather than counted as a pass. The before/after property is genuinely measured only over the ids NOT in that map, and the row that consumes this fixture must assert that set is non-empty.

unmeasurable_under_previous_schema.ojz_sec6_baseswap: the previous schema REFUSES this document (1 issue(s), first: /base_swap: expected object, got array), so it never descended into the migrated key and its canonical output is not a before-half. (For the record the two outputs did happen to agree — which is a fact about the walk falling through, not about the amendment.)
